findings.title: HTTP call lacks proper error handling
findings.explanation: HTTP call to bank transfers service lacks proper error handling. response.raise_for_status() on line 43 will raise an unhandled exception if the debit fails, crashing the request and leaving the system in an inconsistent state (refund succeeded but fee debit failed). Service functions should catch HTTP errors and raise appropriate domain errors.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the _bank.post() call and raise_for_status() in a try/except block. Catch httpx.HTTPStatusError and httpx.RequestError, then raise an appropriate domain error like errors.ProviderUnavailable('bank transfers service unavailable') to allow the API layer to return a proper HTTP response. Consider whether the refund should be rolled back or the fee debit should be retried asynchronously.

findings.title: Potential inconsistency between refund creation and fee debit
findings.explanation: Potential inconsistency between refund creation and fee debit. If the refund succeeds (line 32-34) but the fee debit fails (line 36-43), the merchant gets a refund without being charged the processing fee. No compensation logic or transaction boundary ensures both operations succeed or fail together.
findings.recommendation: Consider one of: (1) Make the bank debit call idempotent using the refund.id as a deduplication key so it can be safely retried if it fails; (2) Move the fee debit to an async background job that retries on failure; (3) Document this as a known limitation and rely on manual reconciliation; (4) Wrap both operations in a distributed transaction pattern (e.g., saga pattern with compensation).
